purpose: Independent isolated runtime parity assessment of psmux 3.4.0 and the installed bridge, with measurements usable to revalidate CONTRACT.md section 14 (steps 5-8: rules 1a/1b/1c/1d/1e/D0).

method.isolation: The probe operator reports that backend invocations were namespaced with -L except read-only list-sessions and -V, and that all cleanup commands targeted the disposable namespaces. A default-namespace session disappeared during the assessment; the retained records do not establish its cause or exclude interference.
method.reads: Geometry read via list-windows/list-panes after each step; each reading polled until two consecutive pane listings agreed (max 6 polls, 300ms apart) instead of a single fixed sleep. Verdicts computed from final stable reads.
method.window: 120 columns (direct arm), default psmux window size on this host. Shares (main_width/window_width) are the comparable numbers.
method.sanitization: Only dummy values used (http://127.0.0.1:59999, ses_probe_a, session p340/p340b). No user data or credentials in outputs.
method.existing_harness_safety: Existing scripts/windows/parity probes scope every invocation with -L <ns> and namespace their kill-server, so they cannot touch default-socket user sessions; but they use FIXED shared namespaces (omo_t19..omo_t24) with preemptive kill-session/kill-server, so concurrent runs could reap each other. Measured minimally with unique disposable namespaces instead; existing probes were read but not executed.

gate_4_4_V_exit_0.reason: Backend and installed shim both answer -V with exit 0.

rule_1a_percent_form.reason: set-window-option main-pane-width "50%" alone left share at 0.5917, but the follow-up untargeted select-layout moved it to 0.4917 with nothing else stored in between (direct steps A -> A2: 71 -> 59 of 120). Same on height axis (F 0.5667 -> F2 0.3667 with only the "40%" form set). On 3.3.8 the follow-up left the share unchanged (CI evidence). The 3.4.0 source and this observation support that the % form is stored. Bridge S1 (strip to bare 50 + injected layout) yielded geometry 59 in this trial.

rule_1b_layout_followup.reason: Storing alone applies nothing (A: 0.5917 unchanged; F-height: 0.5667 unchanged; D2 order claim: layout-then-set-40 leaves 0.4917 unchanged), and the follow-up applies it (A->A2: 0.5917 -> 0.4917; F->F2: 0.5667 -> 0.3667). Bridge-injected follow-up verified in shim call log (followUps reason psmux-reads-main-pane-size-only-inside-apply-layout) and by S1 geometry 59.

rule_1c_resize_cells_suppressed.reason: Direct resize-pane -t <pane> -x 99 on the 120-column main-vertical window yields main width 117 (share 0.975, ~98% of usable width): the cell count arrives as a percentage. Identical argv through the bridge exits 0, is logged kind=suppressed reason=resize-cell-count-is-not-a-percentage, and leaves geometry at 59 (0.4917).

rule_1d_pane_scoped_suppression.result: BEHAVIOR-CHANGE on 3.4.0 (premise false; bridge still suppresses)
rule_1d_pane_scoped_suppression.reason: Direct set-option -p -t <pane> @omo_attach_* now exits 0 with empty stderr (on 3.3.8 it exited 1 with "pane-scoped option ... is not supported"). The URL value is stored: show-options -p -t <pane> reads back "@omo_attach_server_url http://127.0.0.1:59999" with exit 0 (micro-2). Bridge still suppresses its tested URL write (exit 0, logged reason psmux-refuses-pane-scoped-options, no backend call), so the reason no longer describes this backend. Effects on OmO's stale-attach sweep were not measured.

rule_1e_team_resize_rewrite.result: INCONCLUSIVE (backend defect shape holds; through-bridge outcome unresolved)
rule_1e_team_resize_rewrite.reason: Direct resize-pane -t <caller> -x "30%" yielded main width 42 (share 0.35). Through the bridge, exit was 0 and geometry stayed 59 (0.4917); the probe operator reports a call-log record of a rewrite to set-option main-pane-width 30 with a select-layout main-vertical follow-up. In a separate namespace, the recorded direct set-option plus layout control yielded width 35 (0.2917). The retained artifact does not include complete setup, target-window context, or the actual follow-up execution record; the discrepancy is inconclusive and its cause is unknown.

rule_D0_display_F_rewrite.reason: Direct display -p -F "#{session_id}" prints "-F $171" and display -p -F "#{session_name}:#{window_index}" prints "-F p340:0" (client folds -F into message text, as on 3.3.8). Through the bridge both print clean values ("$173", "p340:0") with rewriteReason psmux-client-treats-display-F-as-message-text logged and exit 0.

teardown_dead_pane_wording.reason: kill-pane against an already-dead pane exits 1 with stderr containing "psmux: can't find pane: %3", matching OmO's /can't find pane/i success-on-failure gate (CONTRACT 3.8).

bridge_call_log_excerpts: Operator-reported log summary for the _shim namespace: S1 set-window-option forwarded as bare 50 with a planned select-layout follow-up; S2 resize -x 99 and S3 set-option -p marked suppressed; S4 resize-pane rewritten to set-option main-pane-width 30 with a planned select-layout follow-up; S5/S5b display marked rewritten. Full per-record log JSON is not included in this artifact, and the planned follow-up alone does not establish that it succeeded.

cleanup_proof.sessions_left: [] in all three namespaces (kill-session exit 0; trailing list-sessions exit 1 = no server)
cleanup_proof.remote_temp_files: All probe/result/log/shimlog copies removed from %TEMP%; REMOTE-CLEAN-DONE verified with no leftovers listed.
cleanup_proof.default_socket_note: A session (0: 1 windows, attached) existed on the default socket at the operator's first read-only check; at the final read-only check no default-socket server was running. The operator reports that cleanup kills used -L with the disposable namespaces. The cause of the default session's disappearance is not established by the retained records.

limits: One session, one window, one client, sequential calls; 120-column default window. No multi-window, concurrent-client, or team-layout end-to-end replay (deferred; team probe needs the resolved 1e question first).
The S4/1e discrepancy rests on geometry and reported call-log intent, not a retained execution trace; window targeting and whether the follow-up executed require further investigation.
The disposable probe script and complete call logs were not retained, so this artifact alone cannot independently reproduce the exact setup or establish whether the default namespace was affected.

Rule retirement decisions (CONTRACT 8.2) need more than this artifact. The c20016c and 4addc0a ancestry check was run separately (both are in v3.4.0), but rule 1d stale-attach-sweep effect and rule 1e bridge discrepancy remain unresolved.
